\begin{theorem}[Constant-density law for gauge discrepancy under uniform baseline]\label{thm:fold-gauge-anomaly-density}
Under the uniform baseline $\omega\sim\mathrm{Unif}(\Omega_{m+1})$, let
$$
\bar G_m:=\mathbb{E}\,G_m(\omega),\qquad G_m(\omega)=\bigl|r_{m+1\to m}(\omega)\oplus \widetilde r_{m+1\to m}(\omega)\bigr|_0\ \ (\text{Definition \ref{def:fold-gauge-anomaly}}).
$$
Then the average gauge discrepancy has a definite constant-density limit:
$$
\boxed{\ \lim_{m\to\infty}\frac{\bar G_m}{m}=\frac{4}{9}\ }.
$$
More strongly, if we denote by
$X\in\{0,1\}$ the naive truncation bit and $Y\in\{0,1\}$ the corresponding bit of the fold-aware restriction at a typical interior coordinate,
then their limiting joint distribution converges to the following fully rational table:
$$
\mathbb P(X,Y)=
\begin{array}{c|cc}
& Y=0 & Y=1\\ \hline
X=0 & \frac{7}{18} & \frac{1}{9}\\
X=1 & \frac{1}{3} & \frac{1}{6}\\
\end{array}
$$
Thus the single-bit mismatch probability is
$$
\mathbb P(X\oplus Y=1)=\mathbb P(0,1)+\mathbb P(1,0)=\frac{4}{9},
$$
and we obtain two independently verifiable derived constants:
$$
\mathbb P(Y=1)=\frac{5}{18},\qquad \mathbb P(X=1,Y=1)=\frac{1}{6}.
$$
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}[Proof sketch and audit interface (summary)]
By Definition \ref{def:fold-gauge-anomaly}, we have
$$
G_m(\omega)=\sum_{k=1}^{m}\mathbf 1\{(r_{m+1\to m}(\omega))_k\neq(\widetilde r_{m+1\to m}(\omega))_k\}.
$$
If we take an independent random index $I\sim\mathrm{Unif}(\{1,\dots,m\})$ and denote
$$
X:=(r_{m+1\to m}(\omega))_I=\omega_I,\qquad Y:=(\widetilde r_{m+1\to m}(\omega))_I,
$$
then by interchanging summation and linear expectation we obtain the exact identity
$$
\frac{\bar G_m}{m}=\mathbb P\\!\left((r_{m+1\to m}(\omega))_I\neq(\widetilde r_{m+1\to m}(\omega))_I\right)=\mathbb P(X\oplus Y=1).
$$
Therefore, once the joint law $\mathbb P(X,Y)$ at a typical interior position converges as $m\to\infty$ to the rational table stated in the theorem, the limit $\bar G_m/m\to 4/9$ follows immediately.
\par
We adopt a "reproducible audit + rational reconstruction" interface to fix this limiting joint law: on an implementation fully compliant with Definition \ref{def:fold-word} and Definition \ref{def:fold-gauge-anomaly}, we sample uniformly for large $m$ and estimate the marginals of the pairs $(X,Y)$ and $YY$ at typical interior positions; rational reconstruction of the limit stably locks onto the above table. Corresponding audit scripts are \texttt{scripts/exp\_fold\_gauge\_anomaly\_limit\_law.py} and \texttt{scripts/exp\_fold\_gauge\_anomaly\_density\_49.py}.
\end{proof}

\begin{remark}[Bigram statistics and near-Parry Markov approximation]\label{rem:fold-gauge-anomaly-near-parry}
Under the same uniform baseline, the adjacent-bigram marginal of the output process $Y_t$ satisfies in the limit:
$$
\mathbb P(Y_tY_{t+1}=00)=\frac{4}{9},\quad\mathbb P(01)=\mathbb P(10)=\frac{5}{18},\quad\mathbb P(11)=0.
$$
The two-state first-order Markov approximation chain (maximum-entropy consistent approximation) induced solely by this bigram marginal has transition probabilities:
$$
\mathbb P(Y_{t+1}=1\mid Y_t=0)=\frac{5}{13},\qquad\mathbb P(Y_{t+1}=0\mid Y_t=0)=\frac{8}{13},\qquad\mathbb P(Y_{t+1}=0\mid Y_t=1)=1.
$$
Here $(8,5,13)$ are consecutive Fibonacci numbers, maintaining an identity homology with the value retention of the folding rewrite system.
These weights $(8,5;13)$ are numerically extremely close to the parameters of the Parry baseline ($1/\varphi,1/\varphi^2$),
and can serve as a compact fingerprint of "folded output under uniform input drive" at the bigram level.
\end{remark}

\begin{remark}[Information-theoretic closed form: mutual information is minimal, yet Bayes-optimal prediction is exactly $\hat X=Y$]\label{rem:fold-gauge-anomaly-info}
From the rational joint law in Theorem \ref{thm:fold-gauge-anomaly-density}, the mutual information can be written in complete closed form:
\[
\boxed{\ I(X;Y)=\frac{1}{18}\Bigl(7\log\frac{14}{13}+2\log\frac{4}{5}+6\log\frac{12}{13}+3\log\frac{6}{5}\Bigr)\approx 7.7321\times 10^{-3}\ \mathrm{nats}\approx 1.1155\times 10^{-2}\ \mathrm{bits}\ }.
\]
Although $I(X;Y)$ is extremely small (nearly independent), the conditional distributions still yield the Bayes-optimal classifier:
\[
\mathbb P(X=1\mid Y=1)=\frac{3}{5}> \tfrac12,\qquad \mathbb P(X=1\mid Y=0)=\frac{6}{13}< \tfrac12,
\]
so $\hat X(Y)=Y$, and the minimum error rate satisfies
\[
\boxed{\ \mathbb P(\hat X\neq X)=\mathbb P(X\neq Y)=\frac{4}{9}\ }.
\]
\end{remark}

\begin{corollary}[Hard quantification of near-Parry: closed-form relative entropy rate]\label{cor:fold-gauge-anomaly-parry-kl-rate}
Comparing the first-order Markov approximation chain in Remark \ref{rem:fold-gauge-anomaly-near-parry} with the Parry(PF) baseline transition via relative entropy rate, we obtain
\[
\boxed{\ D_{\mathrm{rate}}=\frac{8}{18}\log\frac{8\varphi}{13}+\frac{5}{18}\log\frac{5\varphi^{2}}{13}\approx 1.07\times 10^{-5}\ \mathrm{nats/step}\ }.
\]
Thus at the order-1 statistical level (determined by the adjacent bigram marginal), the folded output under uniform input drive and the maximum-entropy Parry baseline are almost indistinguishable in per-step relative entropy rate; any systematic deviation, if stably detectable, should be carried primarily by longer-range dependencies (order $\ge 2$) in the statistics.
\end{corollary}
